_doc: AXIS-LEVEL combo expectations for the Commander Spellbook combo-recall bench (ADR 0004 §5, issue #31). REPLACES combo-expected-tiers.json, which stored a per-combo COPY of what the engine produced — a Green/Amber/Missed tier plus a whole `expected` diagnostics block including the winning cycle's limiting hop — and asserted the live run still equalled it. That was a golden-file test with 33 golden files, and it churned on changes with no semantic content: the LimitingHop null-when-nothing-limits fix (776ff939) moved 18 of 33 pins for zero semantic change. WHAT IS PINNED NOW: which AXES hold. Never which hop limited, never a colour. THE DEFAULT IS STATELESS — every eligible combo is expected to satisfy all five ADR-0002 §8 axes (to be a CERTIFIED INFINITE). No entry is needed to say that, so a newly-eligible combo is covered the moment it appears and a silently- degrading one has nowhere to hide. AN EXCEPTION IS {combo, axis, verdict} — the engine computes THAT an axis fails; a human rules THAT the failure is genuine. Only `verdict` is hand-set. NOTHING regenerates it: a gate whose expectation is regenerated from the engine's own output asserts that the engine agrees with itself and can never fail (ADR 0004 §5.2). The gate's failure message prints the exact entry to paste, stamped UNJUDGED, which is itself a hard failure until ruled on. VERDICT VOCABULARY: `genuine` = the axis genuinely does not hold in Magic terms, the engine is right to floor it (judge-attested); `modelling-gap` = the axis fails because the model is coarse, not because Magic says so — known debt, still pinned so it cannot move unnoticed; `carried-over` = inherited verbatim from the pre-#31 pin file, whose prose carried NO judge attestation. `carried-over` is DEBT, not an endorsement: it is the honest statement that this expectation was never independently ruled on, and it is a visible burn-down list for the interaction-judge. HONEST CLASSIFICATION: `axisExceptions` is per-combo state — a NARROWER PIN, not a stateless invariant. `combos` is the eligible-set ROSTER (id + cards): DERIVED, gate-checked against the live run, regenerated by `dotnet run -- --regenerate-roster`, never hand-edited. It is committed only because two CORE-ring consumers (the ADR-0004 §4 quarantine→tier cross-track join and the fidelity blast-radius report) need card→combo without being able to run the interaction engine. `note` IS NARRATIVE ONLY — no gate and no report treats it as truth (ADR 0004 §5.3). The pre-#31 `reason`/`narrative` prose is carried over verbatim onto the first axis exception of each combo (canonical axis order), so nothing is lost; it is NOT machine-checked and may have gone stale. The mechanistic half of that prose is gone: plain-language text is now GENERATED from the axis vector at display time by MagicAST.Interaction.ComboPlainLanguage and stored nowhere. `unreconstructed` PINS THE COMBOS WITH NO RECONSTRUCTION AT ALL (the old `Missed` tier). ADR 0004 §5 / issue #31 intended these to leave this gate for issue #32's derived demand backlog — but #32 DOES NOT EXIST YET, so they stay here rather than being silently dropped (which would remove coverage with nothing replacing it) or moved to a new hand-maintained backlog file (which would create exactly the artifact this ADR exists to remove). They remain load-bearing while they sit here: the gate fails if one of them starts reconstructing (an unannounced coverage GAIN) and fails if a reconstructing combo stops (a regression). WHAT #32 INHERITS: these four combo ids as unserved demand, at which point this section and its gate assertions are deleted.

axisExceptions.note: 2026-07-18 precision-fix investigation (Currency B, following Chatterfang x Pitiless Plunderer -> Green): CONFIRMED honest AMBER, not an engine gap -- do not promote. Both cards' ETB ('you may exile another/target ... permanent/creature you control, then return that card') is an OPTIONAL blink (EffectType=optional, CR 117.7), so PortGraph.cs marks the emit:blink port Gated=true; PortCycle.Firable (ADR-0002 §8) floors ANY cycle touching a Gated port to AMBER regardless of edge Reliability -- verified live (engine.Materialize + FindCycles over the two hand-parsed golds): the 2-hop blink<->etb cycle has Firable=false, LimitingReason='gated (rate-limit / intervening-if)'. Independently, each cross-card blink->etb bridge edge is ALSO Reliability=No/Reason=IsSelf (ObjectFilterRelations.Subsumes on the IsSelf axis): a broad 'another permanent you control' / 'target non-Angel creature you control' blink target can never be proven to hit the SPECIFIC other card needed to fire its self-only ETB (object-identity is a player choice, not a type fact) -- the same object-identity floor as guard:self-watch in kiki-jiki-x-restoration-angel.json (interaction-judge PASS, accretion batch 8, 2026-07-17). Both floors are structural, deliberate (ADR-0002 §8; the general Gated-cycle and IsSelf-Subsumes contracts must NOT be loosened per-card) and already regression-pinned: BlinkFlowArmScopeTest.Felidar_guardian_x_restoration_angel_reconstructs_amber_pure_two_card_blink (tests/magic-ast-tests/Tests/Interaction/BlinkFlowArmScopeTest.cs) asserts this exact combo id (1090-2781, pop 48050) reconstructs AMBER. No interaction gold exists for this pair (kiki-jiki-x-restoration-angel.json witnesses the same shape via a different card pairing), so there is no 'gold ahead of engine' mismatch either. Verified oracle text against oracle-cards.json: Felidar Guardian 'When this creature enters, you may exile another target permanent you control, then return that card to the battlefield under its owner's control.'; Restoration Angel 'When this creature enters, you may exile target non-Angel creature you control, then return that card to the battlefield under your control.'

2026-07-18 Green->Amber RE-PIN (data-fidelity correction, not a regression): the 2026-07-18 Amber->Green promotion above was built on a STALE SuturePriest.json fixture whose Input.OracleText read 'Whenever another creature enters the battlefield under your control, you gain 1 life. Whenever a creature an opponent controls enters the battlefield, that player loses 1 life.' (old pre-templating wording, no 'may' anywhere) and TypeLine 'Creature — Human Cleric' — both wrong vs. the real current oracle text 'Whenever another creature you control enters, you may gain 1 life.\nWhenever a creature an opponent controls enters, you may have that player lose 1 life.' / 'Creature — Phyrexian Cleric' (verified byte-exact against Data/_01_Raw/Datasets/External/oracle-cards.json). Correcting the fixture and re-deriving Output via the real parser (added MayHaveThatPlayerLoseLifeRule.cs for the bare optional-loseLife shape; YouGainLifeRule already handled the optional gainLife shape) now wraps Suture Priest's life-gain trigger in an OptionalEffect. Per PortGraph.cs's 'optional' case, an OptionalEffect-wrapped port is Gated=true, and per PortGraphEngine.cs Firable / ADR-0002 §8, any Gated port on a cycle floors it to Amber. Empirically confirmed via `dotnet test tools/bench/MagicAtlas.Bench` (261-2577-5670 is the only failure against the prior Green pin; all other 72 pinned combos, including the other 2026-07-18 life-cost promotions, are unaffected). This is the honest result: the earlier Green rested on wrong card text; correcting the text correctly demotes it. The underlying LifeCostToPay bridge and cycle topology (Gravecrawler recast -> Suture Priest ETB trigger -> life-gain -> Warren pay:paylife -> Treasure -> sac -> mana:any -> Gravecrawler recast) are unchanged and still traced/mana-balanced; only the life-gain port's certainty tier changed now that it is honestly optional. The general 'any Gated port floors to Amber' policy is intentionally NOT touched here — out of scope for this fix.

2026-07-18 audit (confirmed no-op, correctly Amber): materialized the 3-card graph directly (PortWalk + PortGraphEngine). The engine reconstructs the SAME 2-card 4-hop cycle as the sibling 1385-3000-5670 (Warren x Zulaport x Chatterfang) combo -- Chatterfang's Squirrel token -> Warren's 'Sacrifice another creature' -> Warren's Treasure -> Chatterfang's token-doubling replace -> back to a Squirrel token -- with every hop already Reliability=Yes/Tier=Green (Warren's sac-cost fodder filter declares CardTypes:[creature] directly, so the 2026-07-18 Chatterfang x Pitiless Plunderer Squirrel-subtype fix is a no-op here too). CycleCards confirms Academy Manufactor sits OUTSIDE the reconstructed cycle, exactly like Zulaport in the sibling combo. The sole limiter is the SAME structural gap: CoCostsSatisfied=false ('unfed co-cost') on Warren::pay:paylife -- no flow arm bridges a life-gain emit to a pay-life cost consume (the engine has no life-cost-vs-life-gain balance dimension; Currency C scope, owned elsewhere this round). UNLIKE the Zulaport sibling, though, Academy Manufactor cannot actually supply that missing life-gain even after a LifeCostToPay bridge lands: its oracle text ('If you would create a Clue, Food, or Treasure token, instead create one of each') is a single replacement whose own Replacement field is itself EffectType=composite (3x createToken: Clue/Food/Treasure); PortWalk's `replacement` branch (PortGraph.cs ProjectEffect, the `effectType == "replacement"` case) calls EmitPort on that Replacement field ONCE rather than recursing into composite children (unlike the top-level ability-effects composite recursion), so the whole triple collapses to one coarse, disconnected `emit:composite` port on Academy Manufactor -- the Food token's intrinsic 111.10b life-gain ability (PredefinedTokens.Registry["Food"] = emit:gainlife, which WOULD project if the composite were recursed) is not derivable from this card at all today. So this specific combo carries a SECOND, narrower, currently-non-limiting projection gap (composite-Replacement collapse) layered under the shared life-cost gap -- fixing the shared LifeCostToPay bridge alone will NOT flip this combo to Green the way it might flip the Zulaport sibling; the composite-collapse gap would also need closing first. Not fixed here (out of this audit's scope; flagging for whoever picks up either gap next). Honest, conservative Amber; not forced to Green.

2026-07-18 precision-fix investigation (Currency B, following Felidar Guardian x Restoration Angel -> confirmed AMBER, 25a93085): CONFIRMED honest AMBER, not an engine gap -- do not promote. Kiki taps to copy Felidar Guardian (Kiki's target filter {creature,!Legendary,Controller:You} Subsumes Felidar's self-type, CopyAdmits); GraftCopyInheritance (PortGraphEngine.cs) grafts Felidar's ports onto the copy under a synthesized copy identity; the copy's own ETB is itself an optional blink that can target Kiki, and CR 400.7 (new object) means Kiki re-enters UNTAPPED when blinked, renewing its {T} -- the blink-to-tap-renewal dual of the inherited-untap arm (copy-inheritance-scope.md Decision 4; Kiki + Corridor Monitor is the GREEN sibling of this shape, 618-4404). THREE independent floors keep this AMBER, verified live by materializing the two hand-parsed golds (two Cycles emitted, both Firable=false, LimitingReason='gated (rate-limit / intervening-if)'): (1) both cross-card blink->etb bridge edges are Reliability=No/Reason=IsSelf (ObjectFilterRelations.Subsumes on the IsSelf axis) -- the same object-identity floor as Felidar+Restoration-Angel and kiki-jiki-x-restoration-angel.json: a broad 'another target permanent you control' blink can never be proven to hit the SPECIFIC card needed to fire its self-only ETB; (2) Felidar's ETB is OPTIONAL ('you may exile...', CR 117.7) so PortGraph.cs marks emit:blink Gated=true, and PortCycle.Firable (ADR-0002 Sec.8) floors ANY cycle touching a Gated port to AMBER regardless of edge Reliability; (3) copy-graft-specific -- the closing blink->tap-self renewal edge is Reliability=Unknown/Reason='inherited untap is optional/conditional' (Decision 3/4, copy-inheritance-scope.md): a grafted closing ability earns GREEN only when unconditional (Corridor Monitor's plain untap -> GREEN, 618-4404); Felidar's inherited blink is optional, so BlinkReachesSource returns Unknown, capping this edge at AMBER too. All three floors are deliberate, general-purpose design (the Gated-cycle, IsSelf-Subsumes, and optional-closing-ability contracts must NOT be loosened per-card) and already regression-pinned: BlinkFlowArmScopeTest.Kiki_x_felidar_guardian_reconstructs_amber_blink_renews_tap (tests/magic-ast-tests/Tests/Interaction/BlinkFlowArmScopeTest.cs) asserts this exact combo id (618-2781, pop 13066) reconstructs AMBER, and interaction-judge already PASSed this exact combo by name: docs/judgments/verdict-2026-06-16-blink.json item 2 ('Kiki-Jiki, Mirror Breaker + Felidar Guardian (bench 618-2781, AMBER) -- copy-inheritance + blink->tap renewal (dual of inherited untap, Decision 4)', verdict PASS). copy-inheritance-scope.md Sec.2's acceptance table predicted this exact target tier (AMBER) before the blink arm even landed. Verified oracle text against oracle-cards.json: Kiki-Jiki, Mirror Breaker 'Haste. {T}: Create a token that's a copy of target nonlegendary creature you control, except it has haste. Sacrifice it at the beginning of the next end step.'; Felidar Guardian 'When this creature enters, you may exile another target permanent you control, then return that card to the battlefield under its owner's control.'

unreconstructed.note: RE-PIN (2026-07-18, was wrongly 'Amber'): the prior Amber never actually used Night of Souls' Betrayal — the cycle the engine found was 'Gravecrawler::emit:returntobattlefield:self => Pitiless Plunderer::sac:artifact:treasure:controlled', i.e. a recast Gravecrawler (a Zombie creature) satisfying a 'sacrifice a Treasure' cost, which is impossible (Gravecrawler is never an artifact/Treasure). That was the exact false-positive the RecastSatisfies subtype guard in d7a8b2c1 (fix(interaction): prune coarse self-return from subtype-specific sacs) correctly pruned; the prune just happened to also remove this combo's only cycle, unmasking that the pin was never verifying the real combo mechanism. The real loop needs Night of Souls' Betrayal's -1/-1 to kill a freshly-recast Gravecrawler via state-based action (1/0 toughness) so it dies-and-recasts with no sac outlet at all; the engine has no P/T-lethality reasoning hop for that ('modifyPT' is an inert port today) per libs/mast-interaction/docs/aristocrat-recursion-scope.md §1 row 2 / §4 Decision 5, which predicted exactly 'AMBER at best, likely Missed... out of scope' for this combo when the recursion arm was scoped. Honest current tier is Missed; upgrading to Amber/Green needs a real P/T-lethality flow arm, not a pin edit.
